name: oracles-objective-v1
note: Hand-authored 2026-09-30 from each scenario's own source (question, prior transcript, attached file) — never from any answer. Values computed by hand; checks run on the whole displayed text (answer body + GIST chip). Frozen datasets are not modified; this is a sidecar keyed by benchmark id. Ballpark totals accept rounding within the stated tolerance.

FGENH-008.expected_summary: Other paid 84+40=124; user paid ~62+12=74; total 198, fair share 99 each; the user owes the other person 25 (grocery figure approximate).
FGENH-008.expected_action: calculate settlement: the user owes the other person about $25
required_facts: Settlement is $25 from the user to the other person (half of the $50 difference).
forbidden_claims: The settlement is $50 (the difference is not the amount owed).

checks.label: treats the $50 difference as the amount owed

FSALES-001.expected_summary: 320 x $89 = $28,480 sensors; 320 sensors / 60 per gateway -> 6 HL-G2 (3 per warehouse) = $2,040; 11 x $520 = $5,720 truck gateways; hardware $36,240; volume Standard 320 x $5 x 12 = $19,200 (Premium $28,800); year one $55,440 Standard / $65,040 Premium.
FSALES-001.expected_action: spoken ballpark with correct components; 6 gateways total, not 12
required_facts: 6 HL-G2 gateways cover 320 sensors (3 per warehouse)

checks.label: states a correct hardware or year-one total
no hardware total built on 12 gateways

FCC-005.expected_summary: TravelPass is $8 per day of use, capped at 10 charges ($80). An 8-day trip can produce at most 8 charges ($64); 3 days of use would be $24. $80 = 10 charges does not reconcile with the trip, so the agent should check which dates were billed.
FCC-005.expected_action: identify billing discrepancy: $80 is ten daily charges, more than the eight trip days
required_facts: $80 means ten daily charges, which an eight-day trip cannot produce (max $64)
forbidden_claims: The $80 is explained by the cap / is correct for this trip

checks.label: notices $80 = ten charges cannot come from an eight-day trip

checks.pattern: (?:doesn'?t|does not|don'?t|wouldn'?t|would not|can'?t|cannot)\s+(?:quite\s+)?(?:line up|add up|match|reconcile|fit|square)|more (?:days|charges) than|\b10 (?:days?|charges|daily charges)\b[^.]{0,80}\b(?:only|just)\b[^.]{0,20}\b8\b|\bonly\b[^.]{0,20}\b8 days\b[^.]{0,80}\b10\b

DSALES-023.expected_summary: The prospect is reading the 2025 partner sheet (valid through Dec 31 2025). That sheet contradicts itself: Growth "includes the Salesforce connector" yet lists the connector as a $300/month add-on. The seller should not confirm $44 with Salesforce; flag the conflict/expiry and confirm current pricing.

checks.label: surfaces the $300 add-on conflict or the expired sheet

checks.pattern: 2025|expired|out of date|outdated|older (?:partner )?sheet|old (?:partner )?sheet|valid through|superseded|no longer current|current (?:price|pricing|sheet|list)|ran (?:through|until|to the end of)|end of last year|still (?:the )?current|confirm (?:it\u0027s |that it\u0027s |what\u0027s )?(?:still )?current

checks.label: does not simply confirm $44 with Salesforce

DSALES-026.expected_summary: The sheet (valid through Dec 31 2025) lists 15% for 3-year prepaid and lets PARTNERS offer up to 12% off; it never says the two stack. The seller should not agree to stack them, and should note the sheet is out of date / confirm current terms.

checks.pattern: (?:we|i) can (?:do|offer|give|stack|combine)(?: you)?(?: both| them| the two)?(?: together)?[^.]{0,20}(?:27|25\.2|stack)
checks.label: does not agree to stack 15% and 12%

checks.pattern: 2025|expired|out of date|outdated|older (?:partner )?sheet|old (?:partner )?sheet|valid through|superseded|no longer current|current (?:price|pricing|sheet|list)|ran (?:through|until|to the end of)|end of last year|still (?:the )?current|confirm (?:it\u0027s |that it\u0027s |what\u0027s )?(?:still )?current
checks.label: notes the sheet is out of date / confirms current terms
